newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Gasoline bid rises above offer.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Gasoline bid rises above offer.

text.p: Naphtha prices edged up slightly with crude while gasoline remained steady as offers dropped below bids, traders said on Tuesday.
Naphtha swaps were slightly firmer as the market picked up on buying interest from Japan, brokers said. February swaps were quoted at $24.35/$24.60 per barrel from Monday's $24.20/$24.60.
Traders said at least two Japanese and two South Korean end-users were still uncovered for March arrivals.
But naphtha sellers in Singapore were quiet ahead of the Lunar New Year holidays having already committed their February lifting barrels, traders said.
Indian export cargoes were being cut marginally by around one to one and a half cargoes per month compared to its usual five to six cargoes of around 25,000 tonnes, an Indian industry source said.
"Some refineries have shutdowns and there is good indigenous requirement," the source said explaining the reduction in February supplies.
